choices.text: The continental plate pushes the oceanic plate down underneath it.
The oceanic plate floats on top because it is thinner
The denser oceanic plate sinks under its own weight - slab-pull - and drags the rest of the plate behind it.
Earthquakes push the oceanic plate down into the mantle

questions.explanation: The trap claim is: The continental plate pushes the oceanic plate down underneath it. In fact Nothing pushes it down: the cold, dense slab sinks under its own weight - slab-pull - and drags the rest of the plate behind it. The denser oceanic plate bends down at the trench and sinks; the continental plate is overridden, not pushing.
questions.misconception: The continental plate pushes the oceanic plate down underneath it.
questions.prompt: Which statement about subduction is correct?

choices.text: It is bigger than the continental plate
Its rock is denser, so it sinks beneath the lighter continental plate
The ocean water weighs it down
It moves faster than the continental plate

questions.explanation: Density decides: oceanic rock is denser than continental rock, so the oceanic plate subducts while the lighter plate rides over it.
questions.prompt: Why is it the oceanic plate that sinks at this boundary?

questions.answer: Nothing pushes it down: the cold, dense slab sinks under its own weight - slab-pull - and drags the rest of the plate behind it.
questions.explanation: Slab-pull is the driver: gravity acting on the heavy sinking slab pulls the whole plate towards and down the trench.
questions.prompt: A student says the continental plate shoves the oceanic plate down. Explain, in two sentences, what actually drives the plate down.

questions.answer: The trench is the deep fold at the surface where the oceanic plate bends down and begins to sink.
questions.explanation: Scene 2 shows the leading edge bending downwards; the trench is the surface sign of that bend.
questions.prompt: In one sentence, say what the ocean trench marks.

choices.text: Trench, earthquakes along the slab, volcanic arc
Volcanic arc, trench, earthquakes along the slab
Earthquakes along the slab, volcanic arc, trench

questions.explanation: Scene 2 forms the trench, scene 3 fires earthquakes along the slab, and scene 4 builds the volcanic arc parallel to the trench.
questions.prompt: Which list gives the features that form along the sinking slab, in scene order?
